lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: communicating a complete and checkable argument
lessonRef.title: Guided practice B: communicating a complete and checkable argument

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read once, then cover the example and try the guided set from memory.

items.prompt: Parallel lines, transversal, one angle 70°. Alternate interior angle?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 34° and 25°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.
In a parallelogram, one angle measures 93°. Find the consecutive angle.
In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 58. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
choices: 29, and it is perpendicular to the third side
58, and it is parallel to the third side
116, and it is parallel to the third side
29, and it is parallel to the third side

items.prompt: A proof concludes that vertical angles are congruent. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
choices: The angles are congruent because they are opposite in position.
The two lines are parallel, forcing the angles to match.
Vertical angles are congruent by definition.
Each vertical angle is supplementary to the same adjacent angle, so both have the same measure.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 85°. Find the measure of the corresponding angle.
In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 44° and 43°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.
In a parallelogram, one angle measures 116°. Find the consecutive angle.
In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 74. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
choices: 37, and it is parallel to the third side
37, and it is perpendicular to the third side
74, and it is parallel to the third side
148, and it is parallel to the third side

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: A proof concludes that the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
choices: The diagonals are congruent, so they must bisect each other.
Alternate interior angles give two pairs of congruent angles, and the opposite sides are congruent, so the triangles formed are congruent by ASA.
Every quadrilateral has diagonals that bisect each other.
The diagonals are perpendicular, which forces bisection.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 76°. Find the measure of the co-interior (same-side interior) angle.
